sections.title: From vele to any noun
sections.content: You know *-val/-vel* from A1 (*busszal*, *Annával*) and from *vele* and *velem*. Here it is again with kitchen tools: it means "with" in the sense of using something, and its "v" still changes to match the sound right before it.

sections.title: -val/-vel in action
rows: with a fork (vowel-final: a becomes á, then -val)
with onion (vowel-final: a becomes á, then -val)

items.english: I eat with a knife and fork.
I eat the soup with a spoon.

sections.content: The pattern: a stem ending in a single consonant doubles that consonant instead of keeping "v" (*kanál* -> *kanállal*, not *kanálvel*); a vowel-final stem just adds -val or -vel, following the same back/front vowel harmony as everything else — and an a-final stem like villa or hagyma lengthens to *á* first, the same lengthening you already know from the accusative (alma -> *almát*).
